prompt: A wheelchair ramp rises $1$ foot for every $1$ foot it runs forward. Its angle is $\arctan(1)$. What is that angle, in degrees?
hint: $\arctan(1)$ asks: which angle has a tangent of $1$?

hints.text: $\arctan(1)$ asks: which angle has a tangent of $1$?
Tangent is rise over run, so you need the angle where rise and run are equal.

explanation: Tangent of the ramp angle is $\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{1}{1} = 1$.
The angle whose tangent is $1$ is $45^\circ$.
So this ramp is at $45^\circ$ — far too steep for a real wheelchair ramp, which is why building codes cap ramps near $4.8^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The isosceles right triangle
steps: Equal rise and run makes an isosceles right triangle.
Its two non-right angles must be equal and add to $90^\circ$, so each is $45^\circ$.
